title: Invariance under small noisy influences
statement:
There is a constant $K>0$ such that for every $n\in\mathbb N$ and every real-valued function $h$ on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ with variance at most $1$, the following holds. If $0<\varepsilon\le1$ and $0<\delta\le1/20$, and every noisy coordinate influence of $h$ at noise parameter $1-\delta$ is at most $\varepsilon$, then for every $c\ge0$ and every $c$-Lipschitz function $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, the difference between the uniform-cube expectation of $\psi(T_{1-\delta}h)$ and its expectation when the Fourier--Walsh polynomial of $T_{1-\delta}h$ is evaluated on independent standard Gaussian coordinates has absolute value at most
\[
Kc\,\varepsilon^{\delta/3}.
\]
